note.question: Are top management teams compensated as teams?
note.overview: Shareholders design performance-contingent contracts for two privately acting managers. The Individual Model explicitly implements joint work as the unique Nash equilibrium against unilateral deviations. The Team Model instead assumes that the managers choose effort jointly and imposes a joint-deviation incentive constraint; it does not derive the internal coordination mechanism as a strategic equilibrium. The paper structurally identifies and tests the restrictions implied by both contracting benchmarks.

sources.quote: Without loss of generality, this specification of g0t(x) can accommodate substitutabil­ ity, independence, or complementarity in production.16 It also has two realistic implications: (1) g1t(x) ≠g2t(x), meaning that each top manager influences the joint out­ put in a unique way,17 and (2) the likelihood under both managers shirking is generally steeper than that under only one manager shirking, meaning that a low realiza­ tion of the performance measure is more likely to appear when both managers shirk than when only one of them shirks.

components.label: Solution or estimation method
components.explanation: The paper first illustrates semiparametric identification in a single-agent moral-hazard model, extends it to two managers, derives optimal-contract and profit-maximization restrictions under the Individual and Team models, nonparametrically estimates compensation and performance distributions, and uses subsampling-based set inference to test whether a common risk-aversion region satisfies each model. It then computes agency-friction measures and a counterfactual switch from individual to team contracting.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: At the beginning of each period shareholders offer each manager a compensation schedule contingent on the joint performance measure. Each manager accepts or takes an outside option and then privately chooses work or shirk. Firm performance is realized conditional on the effort pair, contracts pay, and the relationship repeats through a sequence of short-term contracts. Both models share the same objective and participation constraints but differ in the deviation benchmark encoded by incentive compatibility.

components.label: Unique joint-work Nash equilibrium in the Individual Model
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Unique joint-work Nash equilibrium in the Individual Model; exogenous joint-effort benchmark in the Team Model. In the Individual Model, Equation (14) makes work a best response to a working teammate and Equations (15)-(16) rule out joint shirking as a mutual best response, thereby implementing joint work as the unique Nash equilibrium. In the Team Model, Equation (17) compares joint work with joint shirking after joint effort choice is taken as arising from exogenous production or environmental factors; the paper explicitly leaves repeated-game, strategic, or side-contract implementation outside the model. Proposition 2 derives the optimal contracts, and Sections 5-6 test the restrictions implied by the two benchmarks.
